about: Every WebAssembly instruction the disassembler decodes, with a plain-English description. The opcodes, immediates and stack signatures are in src/core/wasm/opcodes.ts; the text is here.

any.convert_extern.description: Turns a reference that came from the host (externref) into one the module's GC types can inspect (anyref).

array.copy.description: Copies n elements from one array to another (or within one), correctly when they overlap.

array.fill.description: Sets n elements from an index on to a value.

array.get.description: Pops an index and an array reference and pushes the element. Traps on null or an index out of range.

array.get_s.description: Reads an i8 or i16 array element, sign-extended to i32.

array.get_u.description: Reads an i8 or i16 array element, zero-extended to i32.

array.init_data.description: Overwrites n elements of an array with values read from a data segment.

array.init_elem.summary: Fill an array from an element segment
array.init_elem.description: Overwrites n elements of an array with references from an element segment.

array.len.description: Pushes the number of elements of an array. Traps on null.

array.new.description: Pushes a reference to a new array of n elements, each set to a given value.

array.new_data.description: Makes a new array of n numeric elements from the bytes of a data segment, starting at an offset.

array.new_default.description: Pushes a reference to a new array of n zero or null elements.

array.new_elem.summary: Allocate an array from an element segment
array.new_elem.description: Makes a new array of n references from an element segment, starting at an offset.

array.new_fixed.summary: Allocate an array of given values
array.new_fixed.description: Pops as many values as the instruction says and pushes a new array holding them.

array.set.description: Stores a value at an index of a mutable array. Traps on null or an index out of range.

atomic.fence.description: Orders memory accesses: no access before it may be observed after it, and the reverse (sequentially consistent).

block.description: Opens a block that ends at its end. A branch to the block (br, br_if, br_table with its label) jumps forward, past its end: the way WebAssembly writes forward jumps, breaks and early exits.

br.description: Jumps to a label, counted from the innermost enclosing block: 0 is the block it is in. For a block or an if that means past its end, for a loop back to its start, for the outermost label a return.

br_if.description: Pops a condition and branches to the label when it is not zero; otherwise goes on. Loops end with it, and conditions leave blocks with it.

br_on_cast.description: Branches to a label with the reference when it is of the target type; otherwise leaves it and goes on.
br_on_cast.operation: if r is T { goto label }

br_on_cast_fail.description: Branches to a label with the reference when it is not of the target type; otherwise leaves it, cast, and goes on.

br_on_non_null.description: Branches to a label with the reference when it is not null; otherwise drops it and goes on.

br_on_null.description: Branches to a label when the reference on top of the stack is null (dropping it); otherwise leaves it there, now known to be non-null.

br_table.description: Pops an index and branches to the label at that position of the list, or to the last label (the default) when the index is past the end: how a switch statement is compiled.

call.description: Calls a function by its index: pops its arguments (the first deepest) and, when it returns, leaves its results on the stack. Imported functions come first in the index space.

call_indirect.description: Pops an index into a table of functions and calls the function there — how function pointers and virtual methods work. Traps when the slot is empty or the function does not have the expected type.

call_ref.description: Pops a typed function reference and calls it. Traps when the reference is null.

catch.description: Starts the handler for exceptions of one tag inside a try; their values are on the stack.

catch_all.description: Starts the handler for any exception inside a try.

data.drop.description: Tells the engine a passive data segment is no longer needed: memory.init of it traps from now on (except with zero length), and the engine may free it.

delegate.description: Ends a try by handing its exceptions to an outer try, named by a label.

drop.description: Pops a value and forgets it — a function result nobody uses, for instance.

elem.drop.description: Tells the engine a passive element segment is no longer needed; table.init from it traps afterwards (except with zero length).

else.description: Separates the two branches of an if; reaching it from the first branch continues after the end.

end.description: Closes a block, loop, if or try — or, as the last instruction, the function itself, which then returns the values on the stack.

extern.convert_any.description: Turns an internal reference (anyref) into an externref, to hand to the host.

f32.abs.description: Clears the sign bit of a — of a NaN too, without looking at it otherwise.

f32.add.description: Adds two single-precision floats, rounding to the nearest representable value (ties to even), as IEEE 754 prescribes.

f32.ceil.description: Rounds a to an integral value toward +∞; the result is still a single-precision float.

f32.const.description: Pushes the single-precision float whose 4 bytes follow the opcode, exactly — NaN payloads included.

f32.convert_i32_s.description: Converts a signed 32-bit integer to the nearest single-precision float, a tie going to even.

f32.convert_i32_u.description: Converts an unsigned 32-bit integer to the nearest single-precision float, a tie going to even.

f32.convert_i64_s.description: Converts a signed 64-bit integer to the nearest single-precision float, a tie going to even.

f32.convert_i64_u.description: Converts an unsigned 64-bit integer to the nearest single-precision float, a tie going to even.

f32.copysign.description: Pushes a with the sign bit of b: the magnitude of one value with the sign of the other.

f32.demote_f64.description: Rounds a double to the nearest single-precision value; too large a value becomes an infinity.

f32.div.description: Pushes a / b, rounded to nearest. Dividing by zero gives an infinity or NaN, never a trap.

f32.eq.description: Pushes 1 when a == b holds for two single-precision floats, 0 otherwise. NaN on either side makes it 0.

f32.floor.description: Rounds a to an integral value toward −∞.

f32.ge.description: Pushes 1 when a >= b holds for two single-precision floats, 0 otherwise. NaN on either side makes it 0.

f32.gt.description: Pushes 1 when a > b holds for two single-precision floats, 0 otherwise. NaN on either side makes it 0.

f32.le.description: Pushes 1 when a <= b holds for two single-precision floats, 0 otherwise. NaN on either side makes it 0.

f32.load.description: Reads 4 bytes of linear memory, little-endian. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

f32.lt.description: Pushes 1 when a < b holds for two single-precision floats, 0 otherwise. NaN on either side makes it 0.

f32.max.description: Pushes the larger of two single-precision floats. NaN in either gives NaN, and +0 counts as larger than −0.

f32.min.description: Pushes the smaller of two single-precision floats. NaN in either gives NaN, and −0 counts as smaller than +0.

f32.mul.description: Pushes the product of two single-precision floats, rounded to nearest.

f32.ne.description: Pushes 1 when a != b holds for two single-precision floats, 0 otherwise. NaN on either side makes it 1.

f32.nearest.description: Rounds a to the nearest integral value, a tie going to the even one (2.5 → 2.0, 3.5 → 4.0).

f32.neg.description: Flips the sign bit of a, NaN included.

f32.reinterpret_i32.description: Pushes the 32 bits of an integer unchanged, as a float.

f32.sqrt.description: Pushes the square root of a, correctly rounded; NaN for a negative number (−0 gives −0).

f32.store.description: Pops a value and an address and writes the value (4 bytes, little-endian) to linear memory. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

f32.sub.description: Pushes a − b (a is the value below, b the one on top), rounded to nearest.

f32.trunc.description: Drops the fraction of a, keeping an integral float.

f32x4.abs.description: Clears the sign bit of each of the four single-precision lanes.

f32x4.add.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of four single-precision lanes: adds the lanes of two vectors.

f32x4.neg.description: Negates each of the four single-precision lanes (flips its sign bit).

f32x4.pmax.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of four single-precision lanes: takes b where a < b and a otherwise.

f32x4.pmin.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of four single-precision lanes: takes b where b < a and a otherwise — C's ternary minimum, cheap on x86.

i31.get_s.description: Pushes the 31-bit integer inside an i31ref, sign-extended to 32 bits. Traps on null.

i31.get_u.description: Pushes the 31-bit integer inside an i31ref, zero-extended to 32 bits. Traps on null.

i32.add.description: Pops two 32-bit integers and pushes their sum, wrapped modulo 2^32: an overflow is neither trapped nor reported. The same instruction serves signed and unsigned numbers.

i32.and.description: Pushes the bits set in both a and b.

i32.atomic.load.description: Reads 32 bits of shared memory atomically and in sequentially consistent order. Traps unless the address is aligned to the size.

i32.atomic.load16_u.description: Reads 16 bits of shared memory atomically and in sequentially consistent order, zero-extended to i32. Traps unless the address is aligned to the size.

i32.atomic.load8_u.description: Reads 8 bits of shared memory atomically and in sequentially consistent order, zero-extended to i32. Traps unless the address is aligned to the size.

i32.atomic.rmw.add.description: Atomically reads the 32-bit value at an address, adds the operand to it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw.and.description: Atomically reads the 32-bit value at an address, ANDs the operand into it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw.cmpxchg.description: Atomically compares the 32-bit value at an address with an expected one and, when they are equal, writes the new value; pushes the old value either way.

i32.atomic.rmw.or.description: Atomically reads the 32-bit value at an address, ORs the operand into it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw.sub.description: Atomically reads the 32-bit value at an address, subtracts the operand from it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw.xchg.description: Atomically reads the 32-bit value at an address, replaces it with the operand, writes the result back, and pushes the old value. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw.xor.description: Atomically reads the 32-bit value at an address, XORs the operand into it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw16.add_u.description: Atomically reads the 16-bit value at an address, adds the operand to it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i32. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw16.and_u.description: Atomically reads the 16-bit value at an address, ANDs the operand into it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i32. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw16.cmpxchg_u.summary: Atomic compare and exchange (16 bits, i32)
i32.atomic.rmw16.cmpxchg_u.description: Atomically compares the 16-bit value at an address with an expected one and, when they are equal, writes the new value; pushes the old value either way, zero-extended to i32.

i32.atomic.rmw16.or_u.description: Atomically reads the 16-bit value at an address, ORs the operand into it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i32. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw16.sub_u.description: Atomically reads the 16-bit value at an address, subtracts the operand from it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i32. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw16.xchg_u.description: Atomically reads the 16-bit value at an address, replaces it with the operand, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i32. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw16.xor_u.description: Atomically reads the 16-bit value at an address, XORs the operand into it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i32. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw8.add_u.description: Atomically reads the 8-bit value at an address, adds the operand to it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i32. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw8.and_u.description: Atomically reads the 8-bit value at an address, ANDs the operand into it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i32. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw8.cmpxchg_u.summary: Atomic compare and exchange (8 bits, i32)
i32.atomic.rmw8.cmpxchg_u.description: Atomically compares the 8-bit value at an address with an expected one and, when they are equal, writes the new value; pushes the old value either way, zero-extended to i32.

i32.atomic.rmw8.or_u.description: Atomically reads the 8-bit value at an address, ORs the operand into it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i32. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw8.sub_u.description: Atomically reads the 8-bit value at an address, subtracts the operand from it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i32. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw8.xchg_u.description: Atomically reads the 8-bit value at an address, replaces it with the operand, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i32. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.rmw8.xor_u.description: Atomically reads the 8-bit value at an address, XORs the operand into it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i32. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.store.description: Writes a value to shared memory atomically, in sequentially consistent order. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.store16.description: Writes the low 16 bits of a value to shared memory atomically, in sequentially consistent order. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.atomic.store8.description: Writes the low 8 bits of a value to shared memory atomically, in sequentially consistent order. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i32.clz.description: Pushes how many zero bits a has above its highest set bit: 32 for zero.

i32.const.description: Pushes the 32-bit integer written in the instruction (as a signed LEB128). A constant that is the address of data is how code points at strings and variables in memory.

i32.ctz.description: Pushes how many zero bits a has below its lowest set bit: 32 for zero.

i32.div_s.description: Divides a by b as signed numbers, rounding toward zero. Stops the program (traps) when b is zero, and when the most negative value is divided by −1, whose quotient does not fit.

i32.div_u.description: Divides a by b as unsigned numbers, rounding down. Traps when b is zero.

i32.eq.description: Pushes 1 when the two 32-bit integers equal, 0 otherwise.

i32.eqz.description: Pushes 1 when a is zero and 0 otherwise — the logical NOT of a value used as a condition.

i32.extend16_s.description: Takes the low 16 bits of a as a signed number and widens it to 32 bits, copying bit 15 into all the bits above.

i32.extend8_s.description: Takes the low 8 bits of a as a signed number and widens it to 32 bits, copying bit 7 into all the bits above.

i32.ge_s.description: Pushes 1 when a ≥ b as signed numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i32.ge_u.description: Pushes 1 when a ≥ b as unsigned numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i32.gt_s.description: Pushes 1 when a > b as signed numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i32.gt_u.description: Pushes 1 when a > b as unsigned numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i32.le_s.description: Pushes 1 when a ≤ b as signed numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i32.le_u.description: Pushes 1 when a ≤ b as unsigned numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i32.load.description: Reads 4 bytes of linear memory, little-endian. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i32.load16_s.description: Reads 2 bytes of linear memory, little-endian, then widens the value to 32 bits as a signed number. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i32.load16_u.description: Reads 2 bytes of linear memory, little-endian, then widens the value to 32 bits with zeros. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i32.load8_s.description: Reads 1 byte of linear memory, little-endian, then widens the value to 32 bits as a signed number. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i32.load8_u.description: Reads 1 byte of linear memory, little-endian, then widens the value to 32 bits with zeros. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i32.lt_s.description: Pushes 1 when a < b as signed numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i32.lt_u.description: Pushes 1 when a < b as unsigned numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i32.mul.description: Pops two 32-bit integers and pushes the low 32 bits of their product — the same bits whether the numbers are signed or unsigned.

i32.ne.description: Pushes 1 when the two 32-bit integers differ, 0 otherwise.

i32.or.description: Pushes the bits set in a, in b, or in both.

i32.popcnt.description: Pushes the number of one bits in a.

i32.reinterpret_f32.description: Pushes the 32 bits of a float unchanged, as an integer.

i32.rem_s.description: The remainder of the signed division a / b; it has the sign of a. Traps when b is zero; the most negative value % −1 is simply 0.

i32.rem_u.description: The remainder of the unsigned division a / b. Traps when b is zero.

i32.rotl.description: Rotates the bits of a left by b places: bits that leave on the left come back on the right.

i32.rotr.description: Rotates the bits of a right by b places: bits that leave on the right come back on the left.

i32.shl.description: Shifts a left by b bits, filling with zeros. Only the low 5 bits of b count: the shift is taken modulo 32.

i32.shr_s.description: Shifts a right by b bits (modulo 32), copying the sign bit into the vacated bits: a signed division by a power of two that rounds down.

i32.shr_u.description: Shifts a right by b bits (modulo 32), filling with zeros.

i32.store.description: Pops a value and an address and writes the value (4 bytes, little-endian) to linear memory. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i32.store16.summary: Store the low 16 bits of i32
i32.store16.description: Pops a value and an address and writes the low 16 bits of the value (2 bytes, little-endian) to linear memory. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i32.store8.summary: Store the low 8 bits of i32
i32.store8.description: Pops a value and an address and writes the low 8 bits of the value (1 byte, little-endian) to linear memory. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i32.sub.description: Pops two 32-bit integers and pushes a − b (a is the value below, b the one on top), wrapped modulo 2^32.

i32.trunc_f32_s.description: Converts a float to a signed 32-bit integer, dropping the fraction. Traps when the value is NaN or does not fit.

i32.trunc_f32_u.description: Converts a float to an unsigned 32-bit integer, dropping the fraction. Traps when the value is NaN or does not fit.

i32.trunc_f64_s.description: Converts a float to a signed 32-bit integer, dropping the fraction. Traps when the value is NaN or does not fit.

i32.trunc_f64_u.description: Converts a float to an unsigned 32-bit integer, dropping the fraction. Traps when the value is NaN or does not fit.

i32.trunc_sat_f32_s.summary: Saturating truncate f32 to signed i32
i32.trunc_sat_f32_s.description: Converts a float to a signed 32-bit integer, dropping the fraction, without ever trapping: a value too large becomes the largest integer, too small the smallest, NaN becomes 0.

i32.trunc_sat_f32_u.summary: Saturating truncate f32 to unsigned i32
i32.trunc_sat_f32_u.description: Converts a float to an unsigned 32-bit integer, dropping the fraction, without ever trapping: a value too large becomes the largest integer, too small the smallest, NaN becomes 0.

i32.trunc_sat_f64_s.summary: Saturating truncate f64 to signed i32
i32.trunc_sat_f64_s.description: Converts a float to a signed 32-bit integer, dropping the fraction, without ever trapping: a value too large becomes the largest integer, too small the smallest, NaN becomes 0.

i32.trunc_sat_f64_u.summary: Saturating truncate f64 to unsigned i32
i32.trunc_sat_f64_u.description: Converts a float to an unsigned 32-bit integer, dropping the fraction, without ever trapping: a value too large becomes the largest integer, too small the smallest, NaN becomes 0.

i32.wrap_i64.description: Keeps the low 32 bits of a 64-bit integer.

i32.xor.description: Pushes the bits set in exactly one of a and b. With −1 as b it inverts every bit.

i32x4.abs.description: Takes the absolute value of each of the four 32-bit integer lanes; the most negative value stays as it is.

i32x4.add.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of four 32-bit integer lanes: adds the lanes of two vectors, wrapping around.

i32x4.all_true.description: Pushes 1 when every one of the four 32-bit integer lanes is non-zero, 0 otherwise.

i32x4.bitmask.description: Collects the top (sign) bit of each of the four 32-bit integer lanes into the low bits of an i32.

i32x4.dot_i16x8_s.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of four 32-bit integer lanes: multiplies the signed 16-bit lanes and adds neighbouring products into 32-bit lanes.

i32x4.eq.description: Compares the four 32-bit integer lanes of two vectors and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a == b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i32x4.extadd_pairwise_i16x8_s.description: Adds each pair of neighbouring i16x8 lanes into one lane twice as wide.

i32x4.extadd_pairwise_i16x8_u.description: Adds each pair of neighbouring i16x8 lanes into one lane twice as wide.

i32x4.extend_high_i16x8_s.summary: Extend the high half of i16x8 (signed)
i32x4.extend_high_i16x8_s.description: Widens the high half of the lanes of a vector to lanes twice as wide, sign-extending each.

i32x4.extend_high_i16x8_u.summary: Extend the high half of i16x8 (unsigned)
i32x4.extend_high_i16x8_u.description: Widens the high half of the lanes of a vector to lanes twice as wide, zero-extending each.

i32x4.extend_low_i16x8_s.summary: Extend the low half of i16x8 (signed)
i32x4.extend_low_i16x8_s.description: Widens the low half of the lanes of a vector to lanes twice as wide, sign-extending each.

i32x4.extend_low_i16x8_u.summary: Extend the low half of i16x8 (unsigned)
i32x4.extend_low_i16x8_u.description: Widens the low half of the lanes of a vector to lanes twice as wide, zero-extending each.

i32x4.extmul_high_i16x8_s.description: Multiplies the high halves of the lanes of two i16x8 vectors into full-width products, lanes twice as wide.

i32x4.extmul_high_i16x8_u.description: Multiplies the high halves of the lanes of two i16x8 vectors into full-width products, lanes twice as wide.

i32x4.extmul_low_i16x8_s.description: Multiplies the low halves of the lanes of two i16x8 vectors into full-width products, lanes twice as wide.

i32x4.extmul_low_i16x8_u.description: Multiplies the low halves of the lanes of two i16x8 vectors into full-width products, lanes twice as wide.

i32x4.extract_lane.description: Pushes one lane of a vector, chosen by the immediate.

i32x4.ge_s.description: Compares the four 32-bit integer lanes of two vectors as signed numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a >= b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i32x4.ge_u.description: Compares the four 32-bit integer lanes of two vectors as unsigned numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a >= b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i32x4.gt_s.description: Compares the four 32-bit integer lanes of two vectors as signed numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a > b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i32x4.gt_u.description: Compares the four 32-bit integer lanes of two vectors as unsigned numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a > b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i32x4.le_s.description: Compares the four 32-bit integer lanes of two vectors as signed numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a <= b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i32x4.le_u.description: Compares the four 32-bit integer lanes of two vectors as unsigned numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a <= b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i32x4.lt_s.description: Compares the four 32-bit integer lanes of two vectors as signed numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a < b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i32x4.lt_u.description: Compares the four 32-bit integer lanes of two vectors as unsigned numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a < b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i32x4.max_s.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of four 32-bit integer lanes: takes the larger of each pair of lanes as signed numbers.

i32x4.max_u.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of four 32-bit integer lanes: takes the larger of each pair of lanes as unsigned numbers.

i32x4.min_s.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of four 32-bit integer lanes: takes the smaller of each pair of lanes as signed numbers.

i32x4.min_u.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of four 32-bit integer lanes: takes the smaller of each pair of lanes as unsigned numbers.

i32x4.mul.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of four 32-bit integer lanes: multiplies the lanes of two vectors, keeping the low bits.

i32x4.ne.description: Compares the four 32-bit integer lanes of two vectors and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a != b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i32x4.neg.description: Negates each of the four 32-bit integer lanes, wrapping around.

i32x4.relaxed_dot_i8x16_i7x16_add_s.summary: Relaxed dot product of bytes, accumulate
i32x4.relaxed_dot_i8x16_i7x16_add_s.description: Multiplies bytes of a and b (b meant to be 7-bit), adds each group of four products and accumulates into the 32-bit lanes of c.

i32x4.relaxed_laneselect.description: Picks each lane from a or b by a mask whose lanes are all ones or all zeros; for other masks the result depends on the processor.

i32x4.relaxed_trunc_f32x4_s.description: Converts float lanes to signed 32-bit integers; values out of range and NaN give whatever the processor's instruction gives.

i32x4.relaxed_trunc_f32x4_u.description: Converts float lanes to unsigned 32-bit integers; values out of range and NaN give whatever the processor's instruction gives.

i32x4.relaxed_trunc_f64x2_s_zero.description: Converts float lanes to signed 32-bit integers; values out of range and NaN give whatever the processor's instruction gives. The upper two lanes are zero.

i32x4.relaxed_trunc_f64x2_u_zero.description: Converts float lanes to unsigned 32-bit integers; values out of range and NaN give whatever the processor's instruction gives. The upper two lanes are zero.

i32x4.replace_lane.description: Pushes a copy of a vector with one lane, chosen by the immediate, replaced by a scalar.

i32x4.shl.description: Shifts each of the four 32-bit integer lanes by the same scalar amount, taken modulo 32, filling with zeros.

i32x4.shr_s.description: Shifts each of the four 32-bit integer lanes by the same scalar amount, taken modulo 32, copying the sign bit.

i32x4.shr_u.description: Shifts each of the four 32-bit integer lanes by the same scalar amount, taken modulo 32, filling with zeros.

i32x4.splat.description: Copies a scalar into all four 32-bit integer lanes of a new vector.

i32x4.sub.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of four 32-bit integer lanes: subtracts the lanes of b from those of a.

i32x4.trunc_sat_f32x4_s.description: Converts float lanes to signed 32-bit integers, clamping values out of range and turning NaN into 0.

i32x4.trunc_sat_f32x4_u.description: Converts float lanes to unsigned 32-bit integers, clamping values out of range and turning NaN into 0.

i32x4.trunc_sat_f64x2_s_zero.description: Converts float lanes to signed 32-bit integers, clamping values out of range and turning NaN into 0; the two upper lanes of the result are zero.

i32x4.trunc_sat_f64x2_u_zero.description: Converts float lanes to unsigned 32-bit integers, clamping values out of range and turning NaN into 0; the two upper lanes of the result are zero.

i64.add.description: Pops two 64-bit integers and pushes their sum, wrapped modulo 2^64: an overflow is neither trapped nor reported. The same instruction serves signed and unsigned numbers.

i64.add128.description: Adds two 128-bit integers, each given as two i64 halves (low first), and pushes the two halves of the sum, wrapped modulo 2^128.

i64.and.description: Pushes the bits set in both a and b.

i64.atomic.load.description: Reads 64 bits of shared memory atomically and in sequentially consistent order. Traps unless the address is aligned to the size.

i64.atomic.load16_u.description: Reads 16 bits of shared memory atomically and in sequentially consistent order, zero-extended to i64. Traps unless the address is aligned to the size.

i64.atomic.load32_u.description: Reads 32 bits of shared memory atomically and in sequentially consistent order, zero-extended to i64. Traps unless the address is aligned to the size.

i64.atomic.load8_u.description: Reads 8 bits of shared memory atomically and in sequentially consistent order, zero-extended to i64. Traps unless the address is aligned to the size.

i64.atomic.rmw.add.description: Atomically reads the 64-bit value at an address, adds the operand to it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i64.atomic.rmw.and.description: Atomically reads the 64-bit value at an address, ANDs the operand into it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i64.atomic.rmw8.cmpxchg_u.description: Atomically compares the 8-bit value at an address with an expected one and, when they are equal, writes the new value; pushes the old value either way, zero-extended to i64.

i64.atomic.rmw8.or_u.description: Atomically reads the 8-bit value at an address, ORs the operand into it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i64. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i64.atomic.rmw8.sub_u.description: Atomically reads the 8-bit value at an address, subtracts the operand from it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i64. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i64.atomic.rmw8.xchg_u.description: Atomically reads the 8-bit value at an address, replaces it with the operand, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i64. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i64.atomic.rmw8.xor_u.description: Atomically reads the 8-bit value at an address, XORs the operand into it, writes the result back, and pushes the old value, zero-extended to i64. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i64.atomic.store.description: Writes a value to shared memory atomically, in sequentially consistent order. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i64.atomic.store16.description: Writes the low 16 bits of a value to shared memory atomically, in sequentially consistent order. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i64.atomic.store32.description: Writes the low 32 bits of a value to shared memory atomically, in sequentially consistent order. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i64.atomic.store8.description: Writes the low 8 bits of a value to shared memory atomically, in sequentially consistent order. Traps unless the address is aligned.

i64.clz.description: Pushes how many zero bits a has above its highest set bit: 64 for zero.

i64.const.description: Pushes the 64-bit integer written in the instruction (as a signed LEB128). A constant that is the address of data is how code points at strings and variables in memory.

i64.ctz.description: Pushes how many zero bits a has below its lowest set bit: 64 for zero.

i64.div_s.description: Divides a by b as signed numbers, rounding toward zero. Stops the program (traps) when b is zero, and when the most negative value is divided by −1, whose quotient does not fit.

i64.div_u.description: Divides a by b as unsigned numbers, rounding down. Traps when b is zero.

i64.eq.description: Pushes 1 when the two 64-bit integers equal, 0 otherwise.

i64.eqz.description: Pushes 1 when a is zero and 0 otherwise — the logical NOT of a value used as a condition.

i64.extend16_s.description: Takes the low 16 bits of a as a signed number and widens it to 64 bits, copying bit 15 into all the bits above.

i64.extend32_s.description: Takes the low 32 bits of a as a signed number and widens it to 64 bits, copying bit 31 into all the bits above.

i64.extend8_s.description: Takes the low 8 bits of a as a signed number and widens it to 64 bits, copying bit 7 into all the bits above.

i64.extend_i32_s.description: Widens a 32-bit integer to 64 bits as a signed number: the sign bit fills the upper half.

i64.extend_i32_u.description: Widens a 32-bit integer to 64 bits as an unsigned number: the upper half is zero.

i64.ge_s.description: Pushes 1 when a ≥ b as signed numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i64.ge_u.description: Pushes 1 when a ≥ b as unsigned numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i64.gt_s.description: Pushes 1 when a > b as signed numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i64.gt_u.description: Pushes 1 when a > b as unsigned numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i64.le_s.description: Pushes 1 when a ≤ b as signed numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i64.le_u.description: Pushes 1 when a ≤ b as unsigned numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i64.load.description: Reads 8 bytes of linear memory, little-endian. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i64.load16_s.description: Reads 2 bytes of linear memory, little-endian, then widens the value to 64 bits as a signed number. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i64.load16_u.description: Reads 2 bytes of linear memory, little-endian, then widens the value to 64 bits with zeros. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i64.load32_s.description: Reads 4 bytes of linear memory, little-endian, then widens the value to 64 bits as a signed number. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i64.load32_u.description: Reads 4 bytes of linear memory, little-endian, then widens the value to 64 bits with zeros. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i64.load8_s.description: Reads 1 byte of linear memory, little-endian, then widens the value to 64 bits as a signed number. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i64.load8_u.description: Reads 1 byte of linear memory, little-endian, then widens the value to 64 bits with zeros. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i64.lt_s.description: Pushes 1 when a < b as signed numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i64.lt_u.description: Pushes 1 when a < b as unsigned numbers (a is the value below, b the one on top), 0 otherwise.

i64.mul.description: Pops two 64-bit integers and pushes the low 64 bits of their product — the same bits whether the numbers are signed or unsigned.

i64.mul_wide_s.description: Multiplies two i64 as signed numbers and pushes the full 128-bit product as its low and high halves.

i64.mul_wide_u.description: Multiplies two i64 as unsigned numbers and pushes the full 128-bit product as its low and high halves.

i64.ne.description: Pushes 1 when the two 64-bit integers differ, 0 otherwise.

i64.or.description: Pushes the bits set in a, in b, or in both.

i64.popcnt.description: Pushes the number of one bits in a.

i64.reinterpret_f64.description: Pushes the 64 bits of a double unchanged, as an integer.

i64.rem_s.description: The remainder of the signed division a / b; it has the sign of a. Traps when b is zero; the most negative value % −1 is simply 0.

i64.rem_u.description: The remainder of the unsigned division a / b. Traps when b is zero.

i64.rotl.description: Rotates the bits of a left by b places: bits that leave on the left come back on the right.

i64.rotr.description: Rotates the bits of a right by b places: bits that leave on the right come back on the left.

i64.shl.description: Shifts a left by b bits, filling with zeros. Only the low 6 bits of b count: the shift is taken modulo 64.

i64.shr_s.description: Shifts a right by b bits (modulo 64), copying the sign bit into the vacated bits: a signed division by a power of two that rounds down.

i64.shr_u.description: Shifts a right by b bits (modulo 64), filling with zeros.

i64.store.description: Pops a value and an address and writes the value (8 bytes, little-endian) to linear memory. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i64.store16.summary: Store the low 16 bits of i64
i64.store16.description: Pops a value and an address and writes the low 16 bits of the value (2 bytes, little-endian) to linear memory. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i64.store32.summary: Store the low 32 bits of i64
i64.store32.description: Pops a value and an address and writes the low 32 bits of the value (4 bytes, little-endian) to linear memory. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i64.store8.summary: Store the low 8 bits of i64
i64.store8.description: Pops a value and an address and writes the low 8 bits of the value (1 byte, little-endian) to linear memory. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

i64.sub.description: Pops two 64-bit integers and pushes a − b (a is the value below, b the one on top), wrapped modulo 2^64.

i64.sub128.description: Subtracts two 128-bit integers given as pairs of i64 halves and pushes the low and high halves of the difference.

i64.trunc_f32_s.description: Converts a float to a signed 64-bit integer, dropping the fraction. Traps when the value is NaN or does not fit.

i64.trunc_f32_u.description: Converts a float to an unsigned 64-bit integer, dropping the fraction. Traps when the value is NaN or does not fit.

i64.trunc_f64_s.description: Converts a float to a signed 64-bit integer, dropping the fraction. Traps when the value is NaN or does not fit.

i64.trunc_f64_u.description: Converts a float to an unsigned 64-bit integer, dropping the fraction. Traps when the value is NaN or does not fit.

i64.trunc_sat_f32_s.summary: Saturating truncate f32 to signed i64
i64.trunc_sat_f32_s.description: Converts a float to a signed 64-bit integer, dropping the fraction, without ever trapping: a value too large becomes the largest integer, too small the smallest, NaN becomes 0.

i64.trunc_sat_f32_u.summary: Saturating truncate f32 to unsigned i64
i64.trunc_sat_f32_u.description: Converts a float to an unsigned 64-bit integer, dropping the fraction, without ever trapping: a value too large becomes the largest integer, too small the smallest, NaN becomes 0.

i64.trunc_sat_f64_s.summary: Saturating truncate f64 to signed i64
i64.trunc_sat_f64_s.description: Converts a float to a signed 64-bit integer, dropping the fraction, without ever trapping: a value too large becomes the largest integer, too small the smallest, NaN becomes 0.

i64.trunc_sat_f64_u.summary: Saturating truncate f64 to unsigned i64
i64.trunc_sat_f64_u.description: Converts a float to an unsigned 64-bit integer, dropping the fraction, without ever trapping: a value too large becomes the largest integer, too small the smallest, NaN becomes 0.

i64.xor.description: Pushes the bits set in exactly one of a and b. With −1 as b it inverts every bit.

i64x2.abs.description: Takes the absolute value of each of the two 64-bit integer lanes; the most negative value stays as it is.

i64x2.add.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of two 64-bit integer lanes: adds the lanes of two vectors, wrapping around.

i64x2.all_true.description: Pushes 1 when every one of the two 64-bit integer lanes is non-zero, 0 otherwise.

i64x2.bitmask.description: Collects the top (sign) bit of each of the two 64-bit integer lanes into the low bits of an i32.

i64x2.eq.description: Compares the two 64-bit integer lanes of two vectors and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a == b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i64x2.extend_high_i32x4_s.summary: Extend the high half of i32x4 (signed)
i64x2.extend_high_i32x4_s.description: Widens the high half of the lanes of a vector to lanes twice as wide, sign-extending each.

i64x2.extend_high_i32x4_u.summary: Extend the high half of i32x4 (unsigned)
i64x2.extend_high_i32x4_u.description: Widens the high half of the lanes of a vector to lanes twice as wide, zero-extending each.

i64x2.extend_low_i32x4_s.summary: Extend the low half of i32x4 (signed)
i64x2.extend_low_i32x4_s.description: Widens the low half of the lanes of a vector to lanes twice as wide, sign-extending each.

i64x2.extend_low_i32x4_u.summary: Extend the low half of i32x4 (unsigned)
i64x2.extend_low_i32x4_u.description: Widens the low half of the lanes of a vector to lanes twice as wide, zero-extending each.

i64x2.extmul_high_i32x4_s.description: Multiplies the high halves of the lanes of two i32x4 vectors into full-width products, lanes twice as wide.

i64x2.extmul_high_i32x4_u.description: Multiplies the high halves of the lanes of two i32x4 vectors into full-width products, lanes twice as wide.

i64x2.extmul_low_i32x4_s.description: Multiplies the low halves of the lanes of two i32x4 vectors into full-width products, lanes twice as wide.

i64x2.extmul_low_i32x4_u.description: Multiplies the low halves of the lanes of two i32x4 vectors into full-width products, lanes twice as wide.

i64x2.extract_lane.description: Pushes one lane of a vector, chosen by the immediate.

i64x2.ge_s.description: Compares the two 64-bit integer lanes of two vectors as signed numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a >= b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i64x2.gt_s.description: Compares the two 64-bit integer lanes of two vectors as signed numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a > b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i64x2.le_s.description: Compares the two 64-bit integer lanes of two vectors as signed numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a <= b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i64x2.lt_s.description: Compares the two 64-bit integer lanes of two vectors as signed numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a < b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i64x2.mul.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of two 64-bit integer lanes: multiplies the lanes of two vectors, keeping the low bits.

i64x2.ne.description: Compares the two 64-bit integer lanes of two vectors and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a != b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i64x2.neg.description: Negates each of the two 64-bit integer lanes, wrapping around.

i64x2.relaxed_laneselect.description: Picks each lane from a or b by a mask whose lanes are all ones or all zeros; for other masks the result depends on the processor.

i64x2.replace_lane.description: Pushes a copy of a vector with one lane, chosen by the immediate, replaced by a scalar.

i64x2.shl.description: Shifts each of the two 64-bit integer lanes by the same scalar amount, taken modulo 64, filling with zeros.

i64x2.shr_s.description: Shifts each of the two 64-bit integer lanes by the same scalar amount, taken modulo 64, copying the sign bit.

i64x2.shr_u.description: Shifts each of the two 64-bit integer lanes by the same scalar amount, taken modulo 64, filling with zeros.

i64x2.splat.description: Copies a scalar into all two 64-bit integer lanes of a new vector.

i64x2.sub.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of two 64-bit integer lanes: subtracts the lanes of b from those of a.

i8x16.abs.description: Takes the absolute value of each of the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes; the most negative value stays as it is.

i8x16.add.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of sixteen 8-bit integer lanes: adds the lanes of two vectors, wrapping around.

i8x16.add_sat_s.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of sixteen 8-bit integer lanes: adds lanes as signed numbers, clamping the result to the lane's range instead of wrapping.

i8x16.add_sat_u.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of sixteen 8-bit integer lanes: adds lanes as unsigned numbers, clamping at the largest value.

i8x16.all_true.description: Pushes 1 when every one of the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes is non-zero, 0 otherwise.

i8x16.avgr_u.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of sixteen 8-bit integer lanes: averages lanes as unsigned numbers, rounding up.

i8x16.bitmask.description: Collects the top (sign) bit of each of the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes into the low bits of an i32.

i8x16.eq.description: Compares the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes of two vectors and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a == b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i8x16.extract_lane_s.description: Pushes one lane of a vector, chosen by the immediate, sign-extended to i32.

i8x16.extract_lane_u.description: Pushes one lane of a vector, chosen by the immediate, zero-extended to i32.

i8x16.ge_s.description: Compares the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes of two vectors as signed numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a >= b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i8x16.ge_u.description: Compares the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes of two vectors as unsigned numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a >= b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i8x16.gt_s.description: Compares the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes of two vectors as signed numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a > b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i8x16.gt_u.description: Compares the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes of two vectors as unsigned numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a > b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i8x16.le_s.description: Compares the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes of two vectors as signed numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a <= b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i8x16.le_u.description: Compares the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes of two vectors as unsigned numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a <= b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i8x16.lt_s.description: Compares the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes of two vectors as signed numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a < b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i8x16.lt_u.description: Compares the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes of two vectors as unsigned numbers and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a < b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i8x16.max_s.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of sixteen 8-bit integer lanes: takes the larger of each pair of lanes as signed numbers.

i8x16.max_u.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of sixteen 8-bit integer lanes: takes the larger of each pair of lanes as unsigned numbers.

i8x16.min_s.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of sixteen 8-bit integer lanes: takes the smaller of each pair of lanes as signed numbers.

i8x16.min_u.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of sixteen 8-bit integer lanes: takes the smaller of each pair of lanes as unsigned numbers.

i8x16.narrow_i16x8_s.description: Packs the lanes of two vectors into lanes half as wide, clamping each signed value to the signed range of the narrow lane.

i8x16.narrow_i16x8_u.description: Packs the lanes of two vectors into lanes half as wide, clamping each signed value to the unsigned range of the narrow lane.

i8x16.ne.description: Compares the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes of two vectors and sets each lane of the result to all ones where a != b holds and to zero where it does not: a mask for bitselect.

i8x16.neg.description: Negates each of the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes, wrapping around.

i8x16.popcnt.description: Counts the one bits of each byte of a vector.

i8x16.relaxed_laneselect.description: Picks each lane from a or b by a mask whose lanes are all ones or all zeros; for other masks the result depends on the processor.

i8x16.relaxed_swizzle.description: Like i8x16.swizzle, but what an index past 15 gives depends on the processor — whatever its native instruction does.

i8x16.replace_lane.description: Pushes a copy of a vector with one lane, chosen by the immediate, replaced by a scalar.

i8x16.shl.description: Shifts each of the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes by the same scalar amount, taken modulo 8, filling with zeros.

i8x16.shr_s.description: Shifts each of the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes by the same scalar amount, taken modulo 8, copying the sign bit.

i8x16.shr_u.description: Shifts each of the sixteen 8-bit integer lanes by the same scalar amount, taken modulo 8, filling with zeros.

i8x16.shuffle.description: Builds a vector from the 32 bytes of two vectors by sixteen indices written in the instruction.

i8x16.splat.description: Copies a scalar into all sixteen 8-bit integer lanes of a new vector.

i8x16.sub.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of sixteen 8-bit integer lanes: subtracts the lanes of b from those of a.

i8x16.sub_sat_s.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of sixteen 8-bit integer lanes: subtracts lanes as signed numbers, clamping to the lane's range.

i8x16.sub_sat_u.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of sixteen 8-bit integer lanes: subtracts lanes as unsigned numbers, clamping at zero.

i8x16.swizzle.description: Works on a 128-bit vector of sixteen 8-bit integer lanes: picks bytes of a by the indices in b; an index past 15 gives zero.

if.description: Pops a condition: when it is not zero the instructions up to else (or end) run, otherwise those after else. Like a block, a branch to it goes past its end.

local.get.description: Pushes the value of a local variable or parameter of the function — the registers of a stack machine. The most common instruction in most modules.

local.set.description: Pops a value into a local variable.

local.tee.summary: Write a local, keep the value
local.tee.description: Stores the value on top of the stack into a local and leaves it on the stack: an assignment used as an expression.

loop.description: Opens a block whose label is its start: a branch to it jumps back to the top. Reaching its end does not repeat it — a loop only goes round when a br or br_if sends it back.

memory.atomic.notify.description: Wakes up to n threads waiting on an address and pushes how many woke.

memory.atomic.wait32.description: When the i32 at an address equals the expected value, suspends the thread until notified or the timeout (ns, negative for none) passes. Pushes 0 when woken, 1 when the value differed, 2 on timeout.

memory.atomic.wait64.description: Like wait32, for the i64 at an address.

memory.copy.description: Copies n bytes from src to dest, correctly even when the ranges overlap (like memmove). Traps when either range runs outside memory.

memory.fill.description: Sets n bytes starting at dest to the low byte of value (like memset). Traps when the range runs outside memory.

memory.grow.description: Adds n pages to a memory and pushes its previous size in pages, or −1 when it cannot grow (the maximum, or the engine refuses). New pages are zero.

memory.init.description: Copies n bytes of a passive data segment, from an offset in it, into memory at dest. A module with shared memory places its data this way from the start function.

memory.size.description: Pushes the current size of a memory in pages (64 KiB each, unless the memory declares another page size).

nop.description: Does nothing. Rare in compiled code.

ref.as_non_null.description: Leaves a reference on the stack with a non-null type; traps when it is null.

ref.cast.description: Checks that a reference is of the given type and leaves it typed so; traps when it is not.

ref.eq.description: Pops two references (to structs, arrays or i31 values) and pushes 1 when they are the same object, 0 otherwise.

ref.func.description: Pushes a reference to a function of the module — its address, in the sense of WebAssembly.

ref.i31.description: Makes an i31ref, an unboxed small integer that lives inside a reference, from the low 31 bits of an i32.

ref.is_null.description: Pops a reference and pushes 1 when it is null, 0 otherwise.

ref.null.description: Pushes the null reference of a heap type.

ref.test.description: Pops a reference and pushes 1 when it is of the given type (a cast would succeed), 0 otherwise.

rethrow.description: Throws again the exception caught by an enclosing catch.

return.description: Leaves the function, returning the values its type says from the top of the stack.

return_call.description: Calls a function and returns its results, replacing the caller's frame instead of growing the stack.

return_call_indirect.description: A call_indirect that returns the callee's results in place of the caller.

return_call_ref.description: A call_ref that returns the callee's results in place of the caller.

select.description: Pops a condition and two values and pushes the first when the condition is not zero, the second otherwise. Both values have already been computed: a branch-free choice.

struct.get.description: Pops a struct reference and pushes one of its fields. Traps on null.

struct.get_s.description: Reads an i8 or i16 field of a struct, sign-extended to i32. Traps on null.

struct.get_u.description: Reads an i8 or i16 field of a struct, zero-extended to i32. Traps on null.

struct.new.description: Pops the values of all fields and pushes a reference to a new garbage-collected struct holding them.

struct.new_default.description: Pushes a reference to a new struct whose fields are all zero or null.

struct.set.description: Pops a value and a struct reference and stores the value in a mutable field. Traps on null.

table.copy.description: Copies n entries between tables (or within one), correctly when the ranges overlap.

table.fill.description: Sets n entries from an index on to a reference. Traps when the range runs outside the table.

table.get.description: Pops an index and pushes the reference stored at it in a table. Traps when the index is out of range.

table.grow.description: Adds n entries, all set to a given reference, and pushes the old size, or −1 when the table cannot grow.

table.init.description: Copies n references of a passive element segment into a table.

table.set.description: Pops a reference and an index and stores the reference in the table. Traps when the index is out of range.

table.size.description: Pushes the number of entries a table has.

throw.description: Pops the values a tag carries and throws an exception with them; it unwinds to the nearest handler, or stops the program when there is none.

throw_ref.description: Throws again an exception caught earlier as an exnref. Traps on null.

try.description: Opens a block whose exceptions the catch clauses after it handle — the first form of exception handling, which toolchains still emit.

try_table.description: Opens a block in which an exception thrown by a tag the table lists branches to that clause's label (with the exception's values, and its reference for the _ref forms).

unreachable.description: Stops the program with a trap. Compilers put it where control can never arrive — after a call that does not return, at the end of a switch with no default — and for abort and panics.

v128.andnot.description: Keeps the bits of a that are clear in b.

v128.any_true.description: Pushes 1 when any bit of a vector is set, 0 otherwise.

v128.bitselect.description: Takes each bit from a where the mask c has a one and from b where it has a zero: the vector form of select, usually with a compare's mask.

v128.const.description: Pushes the 16 bytes written in the instruction as a vector.

v128.load.description: Reads 16 bytes of memory into a vector. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

v128.load16_lane.description: Reads a 16-bit value from memory into one lane of a vector, keeping the other lanes.

v128.load16_splat.description: Reads one 16-bit value from memory and copies it into all lanes of a vector.

v128.load16x4_s.description: Reads 8 bytes as 4 16-bit values and widens each to 32 bits, sign-extending.

v128.load16x4_u.description: Reads 8 bytes as 4 16-bit values and widens each to 32 bits, zero-extending.

v128.load32_lane.description: Reads a 32-bit value from memory into one lane of a vector, keeping the other lanes.

v128.load32_splat.description: Reads one 32-bit value from memory and copies it into all lanes of a vector.

v128.load32_zero.description: Reads a 32-bit value into the lowest lane of a vector whose other lanes are zero.

v128.load32x2_s.description: Reads 8 bytes as 2 32-bit values and widens each to 64 bits, sign-extending.

v128.load32x2_u.description: Reads 8 bytes as 2 32-bit values and widens each to 64 bits, zero-extending.

v128.load64_lane.description: Reads a 64-bit value from memory into one lane of a vector, keeping the other lanes.

v128.load64_splat.description: Reads one 64-bit value from memory and copies it into all lanes of a vector.

v128.load64_zero.description: Reads a 64-bit value into the low half of a vector whose upper half is zero.

v128.load8_lane.description: Reads a 8-bit value from memory into one lane of a vector, keeping the other lanes.

v128.load8_splat.description: Reads one 8-bit value from memory and copies it into all lanes of a vector.

v128.load8x8_s.description: Reads 8 bytes as 8 8-bit values and widens each to 16 bits, sign-extending.

v128.load8x8_u.description: Reads 8 bytes as 8 8-bit values and widens each to 16 bits, zero-extending.

v128.not.description: Inverts every bit of a vector.

v128.store.description: Writes a vector to 16 bytes of memory. The address is the operand plus the offset written in the instruction; an access that does not fit in memory traps. Any alignment works: the align field is only a hint.

v128.store16_lane.description: Writes one 16-bit lane of a vector to memory.

v128.store32_lane.description: Writes one 32-bit lane of a vector to memory.

v128.store64_lane.description: Writes one 64-bit lane of a vector to memory.

v128.store8_lane.description: Writes one 8-bit lane of a vector to memory.

v128.xor.description: Bitwise exclusive OR of two vectors.
